label: Person
name: Agnes of Jesus
summary:
Agnes of Jesus (1602–1634), born Agnès Galand, was a French Dominican tertiary and mystic whose visions, ecstasies, and reputed miracles attracted wide attention in seventeenth-century France. Born in Le Puy-en-Velay, she entered the Third Order of Saint Dominic and lived an intense spiritual life of prayer, fasting, and mystical experience, reportedly receiving the stigmata and gifts of prophecy.

Her spiritual director was the theologian Jean-Baptiste Vanel, who documented her experiences and promoted her cause after her death. Agnes was beatified by Pope Clement X in 1672, making her one of the prominent French female mystics of the seventeenth century, a period of remarkable mystical flowering in French Catholicism associated with figures like Marie of the Incarnation and Margaret Mary Alacoque.

Agnes of Jesus is remembered primarily in the region of Le Puy and by the Dominican Order, whose tertiary tradition she represented. Her beatification situated her within the Counter-Reformation Church's affirmation of authentic mystical experience as a bulwark against both Protestant scepticism about Catholic spiritual claims and the excesses of quietism. She was canonised by Pope Paul VI in 1978, completing the full recognition of her sanctity.
